options: The compiler cannot infer the return type of `validateToken` without an explicit type parameter in the function declaration.
`validateToken` was imported with the inline `type` modifier, which restricts it to non-emitting type positions and causes a compiler error when used as a value.
Inline `type` imports are restricted to interface and type alias identifiers and cannot be placed before function names.
Module `./auth.ts` must export `validateToken` as a `default` export when consumed alongside type-only specifiers.
objective: Debug compiler errors caused by using identifiers imported via import type in runtime value positions

stem: You are building a client utility that needs the runtime helper `sendRequest` and the interface `RequestConfig` from `./client.ts`. You want a single import statement where tools like esbuild or swc can safely elide `RequestConfig` without stripping `sendRequest`. Which declaration accomplishes this?
options: import type { sendRequest } and { RequestConfig } from "./client.ts";
import { sendRequest, RequestConfig as type } from "./client.ts";
objective: Declare type-only imports (import type) and inline type imports to distinguish types from runtime values

stem:
A developer attempts to combine a default import and named type specifiers in a type-only import declaration:

```ts
import type Client, { ClientOptions } from "./client.ts";
```

Why does the TypeScript compiler disallow this statement?
options: TypeScript requires all default imports to be runtime values and cannot elide default exports during bundling.
The `import type` keyword can only be applied to named import clauses enclosed in curly braces, never default imports.
Bundlers like esbuild require default type imports to use `import { default as Client }` instead.
A type-only import declaration cannot specify both a default import and named bindings together because it is ambiguous whether `type` applies to the default import or the entire declaration.
objective: Declare type-only imports (import type) and inline type imports to distinguish types from runtime values
